title: Mozart: Child Prodigy, Tragic Life
subject: art
description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, an early genius from Salzburg to Vienna, invents the independent composer and leaves an unfinished Requiem.

hero.hook: Six hundred works in thirty-five years: the meteor of Salzburg.

blocks.text: **Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart** (**1756**-**1791**) is the very image of early genius. Born in **Salzburg**, he produced more than **600** works in thirty-five years and transformed Western music.

His life also tells the story of a social shift, from the musician as a court servant to the artist as an independent. That search, costly and fragile, pointed toward [[Romanticism]] and the modern idea of the free composer.

sections.title: The child prodigy on the roads of Europe

blocks.text: Born on **January 27, 1756**, Wolfgang showed extraordinary gifts by the age of three. His father **Leopold**, a violinist and an ambitious teacher, was organizing tours by the boy's sixth year: Vienna, Versailles, London, Rome. Those journeys trained his ear, and he absorbed every musical grammar on the continent.

blocks.caption: The young Mozart on tour: a prodigy shown off to the courts of Europe

blocks.text: In Italy, in **1770**, one feat amazed everyone. After hearing the *Miserere* by [[Gregorio Allegri]] only once in the Sistine Chapel, he wrote the whole score down from memory. The music was protected and copying it risked excommunication, but the prodigy got around the ban. This childhood in a carriage, though, left him without a stable home.
In London in 1764, a scholar from the Royal Society examined the boy. He suspected a trick about his age, so superhuman did the improvising seem.

sections.title: Vienna: the break with the court

blocks.text: In **1781**, Mozart could no longer stand [[The status of the musician in the 18th century]] under **Archbishop Colloredo**. After a famous quarrel, which ended with a kick from the archbishop's secretary, he moved to **Vienna**. It was a historic act: he became one of the first freelance composers.

blocks.caption: The Marriage of Figaro: opera gains a modern psychology

blocks.text: His dramatic genius exploded with *The Marriage of Figaro* (**1786**). He joined [[Freemasonry]] (the “Beneficence” lodge, **1784**), an influence you can hear in *[[The Magic Flute]]*. His **27** piano concertos set soloist and orchestra talking to each other, the summit of [[classicism]]. His handling of money, though, was a disaster.
Mozart loved billiards so much that he owned his own table, a rare luxury. He sometimes composed between two shots.

sections.title: 1791: The Magic Flute and the Requiem

blocks.text: The year **1791** is a paradox: his body was failing, his creative powers were at their peak. He finished *The Magic Flute*, which brought Masonic themes to a wide audience. Then a mysterious messenger commissioned a **Requiem** under a seal of secrecy. Ill, Mozart convinced himself that he was writing his own funeral mass.

blocks.caption: The Requiem: a secret commission and an unfinished work

blocks.text: He died on **December 5, 1791**, at 35. The legend that **Antonio Salieri** poisoned him is romantic; historians point instead to an infection or rheumatic fever. His pupil **Franz Xaver Süssmayr** finished the *Requiem* so that his widow **Constanze** could collect the rest of the fee.
The secret patron was Count von Walsegg, who bought works from composers and passed them off as his own.

sections.title: The myth of the common grave and the legacy

blocks.text: Mozart was buried in a common grave, a practice imposed by Emperor **Joseph II** for reasons of hygiene. It was not an insult: it was the norm for much of the Viennese middle class. **Beethoven** and **Schubert** would later build on his foundations.

events.title: Death and Requiem
events.detail: An unfinished work becomes a myth.

blocks.text: In 35 years, Mozart transformed the symphony, the opera and the concerto, freed himself from the court, and died leaving an unfinished Requiem.
